title: Cambridge IGCSE qualification overview
topic: qualification structure assessment examination sessions grades
content: Cambridge states that IGCSE assessment is at the end of the course and may include written, oral, coursework and practical assessment. Many subjects offer Core and Extended curricula. The page describes A* to G grading and June and November examination sessions, with results in August and January. Subject-specific syllabus rules must be checked separately.

title: Cambridge IGCSE grade threshold tables guidance
topic: grade thresholds component weighting examination series
content: Cambridge explains that grade thresholds are published after each examination series and represent the minimum marks for grades. Thresholds can change between series to account for differences in paper difficulty. Overall syllabus thresholds may use component weighting factors, so candidates must use the correct syllabus and component combination for their exam series.

title: Cambridge International recognition and equivalence in Pakistan
qualification: Cambridge O Level / IGCSE / International A Level
content: Cambridge's Pakistan guidance states that O Level and IGCSE qualifications are equated to the local SSC, while International A Levels are equated to HSSC subject to SSC completion and the requirements for the relevant study group. The page identifies IBCC as the government body responsible for equivalence and advises students to confirm current admission requirements with institutions. Check the latest IBCC rules before giving an individual equivalence decision.

title: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE overview
topic: qualification overview age range international progression
content: Pearson describes its International GCSEs as qualifications designed for international learners, generally aimed at ages 14 to 16, with international subject content and assessment intended to support progression to further study. This overview is not a substitute for the current subject specification, assessment information or qualification-specific grading rules.

title: FBISE revised grading formula notification dated 7 October 2025
issuer: Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education
topic: revised grading formula percentages implementation dates
content: FBISE's 7 October 2025 notification states that the revised grading formula applies from First Annual Examinations 2026 for SSC-I/HSSC-I and from First Annual Examinations 2027 for SSC-II/HSSC-II. The published bands are A++ 96–100%, A+ 91–95%, A 86–90%, B++ 81–85%, B+ 76–80%, B 71–75%, C+ 61–70%, C 51–60%, D 40–50%, and U below 40%. Always check the candidate's level and exam year before applying this table.

title: Turkish Education System: Key Elements, Policies and Reforms (2025)
issuer: Republic of Türkiye Ministry of National Education, Directorate of Strategy Development
topic: upper secondary assessment evaluation grading scale
content: The Ministry's 2025 Turkish Education System report describes upper-secondary exams, performance studies, projects and applications as evaluated on a 100-point basis. Its student-evaluation table lists 85–100 as Excellent, 70–84.99 as Good, 60–69.99 as Moderate, 50–59.99 as Passes, and 0–49.99 as Does not pass. The report summarizes the system and should be checked against current MEB regulations for individual school-year decisions.

title: WAEC e-Learning Data Processing resource page
topic: WASSCE subject resources examiner comments performance
content: WAEC's Data Processing e-Learning page provides subject resources intended to help candidates understand examination standards. The page includes material from several WASSCE examination years and explains that Chief Examiner reviews discuss candidate performance, strengths and weaknesses. Use the linked year and paper-specific material; this page does not establish current WASSCE grading thresholds.
